question.problem: An arithmetic sequence has ${a}_{7}=6$ and ${a}_{8}=-3.$ The common difference of this sequence is $d=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The first thing to note is that the terms are *decreasing*, and therefore we expect the common difference $d$ to be *negative*.

Since the two terms are consecutive, we can find the common difference by subtracting ${a}_{7}$ from ${a}_{8}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}d & ={a}_{8}-{a}_{7} \\  & =-3-6 \\  & =-9\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the common difference is $d=-9.$
